A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSCBM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison despite substantial experimental and layout revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and concept-prediction experiments on CUB, CelebA, and AwA2, alongside ablations, saliency visualizations, and test-time interventions.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on CUB, AwA2, WBCatt, and 7-point, including revised comparisons, component ablations, backbone evaluations, and interventions.

M1.justification: Both versions use CEM embeddings, weighted KNN pseudo-labels, thresholded concept heatmaps, and the same task, concept, and alignment losses. v2 makes visual-encoder inputs explicit in the equations, consistent with v1's existing feature-based description; it does not establish a changed SSCBM procedure.

E1.justification: CUB and AwA2 remain, while CelebA disappears from the reported benchmark results. WBCatt blood-cell classification and 7-point skin-lesion classification add two medical domains with different populations and concept annotations (Section 5.1 and Appendix A.1).

E2.justification: The low-label comparisons replace supervised CBM/CEM baselines with CBM+SSL and CEM+SSL using SSCBM's KNN pseudo-labeling, and add Label-free CBM (Table 2). Appendix Figure 5 also adds fully supervised CBM and CEM intervention curves to the previously SSCBM-only comparison.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation shifts from a 1–80% labeled-data sweep to one labeled example per class and 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% regimes with explicit per-class counts. v2 adds ResNet18/34/50 comparisons and an intervention comparison between 10%-labeled SSCBM and fully supervised baselines. Accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 expands component ablations from one labeling ratio to multiple budgets, replacing CelebA/AwA2 ablations with WBCatt/7-point analyses. Appendix A.3 adds backbone sensitivity experiments. Appendix C adds medical saliency cases and revises the bird examples, while Appendix B expands comparative intervention analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions and average results in Appendix A.2. v2 Figure 5 adds shaded bands around intervention curves, absent in v1, but does not define their statistical meaning. No increase in repetitions or new significance-testing procedure is stated.

E6.justification: The principal result tables are substantially revised. At the nominal 10% ratio, SSCBM's CUB concept/task accuracies change from 91.98%/73.02% to 90.88%/67.67%, and AwA2 from 92.97%/84.20% to 96.48%/89.77%; these are not established same-setting gains or losses. Medical, backbone, baseline, and intervention results are added. In v2 Table 2, Label-free CBM leads CUB task accuracy and CBM+SSL leads AwA2 task accuracy.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the formal latent-code expression by separating h = psi(x) from concept prediction. Section 4.2 changes the written cosine-distance formula from raw inputs to encoded features Omega(x), matching the existing methodological description. These are local mathematical corrections; no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary replace CUB-specific 1%/20% labeling results with a four-dataset claim of average concept/task accuracy gaps of 2.44%/3.93% using 10% labeled data. The central novelty claim—jointly addressing scarce concept annotations and semantic alignment—remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explanation of CelebA/AwA2 fluctuations and adds proposed explanations for Label-free CBM's medical-dataset performance and ResNet50's mixed performance. Appendix B adds interpretation relative to fully supervised intervention baselines. The stated smooth-distribution limitation in Appendix D remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly documents train/validation/test splits for retained datasets and the new medical datasets; this does not establish that retained splits changed. Table 4 corrects CUB's concept count to the 112 already specified in v1's prose. Core implementation settings remain stable, and the 0.6 threshold moves to Appendix A.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for WBCatt, its PBC source dataset, and the seven-point dermatology dataset, while removing the CelebA reference. The related-work discussion and positioning of SSCBM relative to existing concept models and semi-supervised learning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most methodological and related-work prose are retained. v2 revises the abstract, contribution summary, and experimental narrative, adds Appendix A.3, makes local language corrections, and updates authors and affiliations.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Benchmark and ablation tables are substantially reorganized, a backbone table is added, and saliency displays are revised and expanded. Figure 5 gains multiple curves, legends, bands, and new axes. The intervention examples move from v1 Figure 6 to v2 Figure 19.

improvement.justification: Giving CBM/CEM the same pseudo-labeling mechanism and adding Label-free CBM makes v2's central comparison more informative than v1's supervised-only low-label comparison. Medical evaluations and backbone sensitivity also strengthen the evidence. However, Section 5.2's blanket superiority claim contradicts Table 2—for example, Label-free CBM scores 74.31% on CUB versus SSCBM's 67.67% at 10% labeling—and the new uncertainty bands are undefined. These reporting weaknesses limit the net improvement.
